cards.text: Isaac, Abraham's son (Genesis 21:3), is old now, and his eyes are so weak he can't see. He calls in his older son Esau and tells him he's old and doesn't know the day of his death.

cards.question: Isaac has a job for Esau first. He tells Esau to take his quiver and bow and go out into the field. What's Esau supposed to do out there?

answers.text: Hunt some game for his father
Drive a lion away from the flock
Guard the flocks through the night

cards.question: Isaac wants Esau to cook him a tasty dish he loves, so that he can ___ Esau before he dies.

cards.text: But somebody's listening. Rebekah, Isaac's wife (Genesis 24:67), hears what Isaac tells Esau, like that coworker who is NOT listening to your phone call but somehow knows your whole weekend.
Once Esau heads out to hunt, Rebekah goes to her son Jacob, Esau's brother. She tells him what she overheard.

cards.question: True or false: Rebekah tells Jacob to stay out of it.
Rebekah's got a plan, and she can cook what Isaac loves. What does she send Jacob out to the flock to get?

cards.text: She'll make the tasty dish Isaac loves, and Jacob will carry it in so his father blesses HIM before he dies. One problem, and Jacob sees it.

cards.question: Rebekah wants Jacob to carry the dish in and get the blessing meant for Esau. What problem does Jacob see with the plan?

answers.text: Esau is hairy and he is smooth
Goat won't taste like wild game
Esau will be home any minute

cards.question: Jacob says if his father touches him, he could be found out as a deceiver and bring a ___ on himself instead of a blessing.

cards.text: Rebekah answers, "Your curse be on me, my son." So Jacob goes and gets the goats, and she makes the tasty food his father loves.

cards.question: The food's ready. True or false: Rebekah dresses Jacob in Esau's finest clothes.
Good clothes, but Jacob is still smooth. What does Rebekah put on his hands and the smooth part of his neck?

cards.text: Rebekah hands Jacob the tasty food and the bread she made. Goat. On. His. NECK. And he's going in there anyway.
Jacob walks in and says, "My father." And Isaac asks the big one: "Which one are you, my son?"

cards.question: Moment of truth. What does Jacob tell his father, Isaac?

answers.text: I am Jacob your younger son
I am a servant sent by Esau

cards.text: Jacob asks Isaac to sit up and eat his game. Isaac's got a question first: how did he ever find it so QUICKLY?

cards.question: Isaac wants to know how the hunt went so fast. What's Jacob's answer?

answers.text: The LORD your God brought it to me
An angel of the LORD led me to it
My servants drove it right to me

cards.text: Oh, he went THERE. He put the LORD's name on it, and Isaac still isn't sure, so he asks Jacob to come closer so he can touch him.

cards.question: Isaac touches the son who brought him the dish and says the voice is the voice of ___, but the hands are the hands of Esau.

cards.text: Isaac doesn't recognize him, because his hands are hairy like his brother Esau's, so he blesses him.

cards.question: Isaac asks one more time, "Are you really my son Esau?" True or false: Jacob finally comes clean.

cards.text: Jacob says, "I am." So Isaac eats, and Jacob brings him wine, and he drinks.

cards.question: True or false: After he eats and drinks, Isaac asks his son to come near and kiss him.

cards.text: Jacob kisses him, and Isaac smells his clothing, which is Esau's finest. This whole plan is riding on Esau's LAUNDRY.

cards.question: Isaac smells Esau's clothes on Jacob and begins to bless him. What does Isaac say the smell of his son is like?

answers.text: A field the LORD has blessed

cards.text: Isaac blesses him: may God give him the dew of heaven and the richness of the earth, with plenty of grain and new wine.

cards.question: Isaac's blessing over Jacob goes on: may peoples serve him and nations bow down to him. May he be the ___ of his brothers, and may his mother's sons bow down to him.
True or false: Isaac's blessing over Jacob says that those who curse Jacob will be blessed.

cards.text: The blessing's done and Jacob's out the door, and THAT is when Esau gets back from the hunt. You ever walk into the break room, find the cookie box empty, and the crumbs are still warm? Yeah.

cards.question: True or false: Esau comes back from the hunt with nothing for his father.

cards.text: Esau tells his father to sit up and eat his game, so he can bless him. And Isaac's answer is three words: "Who are you?"

cards.question: Esau answers that he's Esau, Isaac's firstborn son. How does Isaac react?
True or false: Isaac says the son he already blessed will be blessed.

cards.text: Esau lets out a loud and bitter cry and says, "Bless me too, O my father!"

cards.question: What does Isaac tell Esau happened to his blessing?

answers.text: Your brother came deceitfully and took it
A stranger tricked me at the door
Your servant brought me the dish first

cards.text: Esau says Jacob is rightly named, because he's cheated him twice.

cards.question: Twice? Esau says Jacob took his ___, and now he's taken his blessing.

cards.text: Esau asks, "Haven’t you saved a blessing for me?" Isaac says he's already made Jacob his master and sustained him with grain and new wine, so what's left?

cards.question: Esau keeps pleading with his father. What does Esau ask next?

answers.text: Do you have only one blessing

cards.text: Then Esau weeps aloud. I think this one hurts, friend.

cards.question: Isaac finally answers Esau's cry. Where does Isaac say Esau's dwelling place will be?

answers.text: Away from the richness of the land
In the well-watered plain of the Jordan
In a land flowing with milk and honey

cards.question: Isaac tells Esau he will live by the ___ and serve his brother.
True or false: Isaac says Esau will serve his brother forever, with no way out.

cards.text: Isaac says that when Esau rebels, he'll tear his brother's yoke off his neck. We'll stop here for now, friend, but this story is far from finished.
